battle.name: 翟松柏起義
battle.brief: 大業十二年（616年）正月初七，雁門郡人翟松柏於靈丘聚眾數萬，攻掠周邊郡縣，隋軍自太原與雁門關一線出師討平。卡面這件秦連弩正是邊郡守城與隘口阻擊的舊式兵器：弩機儲力、一踩一發，靠連續射擊把進攻隊形壓在牆外。

kit.name: 秦連弩
kit.history: 弩機把拉力存起來，一踩一發。守城的一方靠它把攻城的人壓在牆外。

countries: 交戰雙方是隋朝與以翟松柏為首的雁門起義軍。隋朝此時是東亞疆域最廣的帝國之一，開皇年間統一的政治框架仍在，但大業朝已把國家推上崩解的斜坡。煬帝楊廣自604年即位，到616年已十二年，國都洛陽與東都江都之間，巡幸的隊伍沿運河不斷往返。隋的軍權分兩層：中央由尚書省兵部掌軍籍、符印與軍令，前線設行軍總管、總管、判官，郡縣則有太守、令率郡兵、縣兵應敵，北方邊郡另有屯田戍卒與防護兵。大業年間府兵制已名存實亡，開皇時寓兵於農、番上宿衛的編制被連年兵役抽空，府庫空虛、逃戶成了兵源的主要補充，募兵與郡兵混編的隊伍成為實際主力。起義軍方面，是聚在鄉里、以農民、逃戶與市井散兵為主體的武裝，領導核心只有翟松柏一人，沒有可考的幕僚與將領體系。起義中心雁門郡，治所在雁門縣，即今山西代縣，郡下領雁門、靈丘、繁畤、五台、崞五縣，靈丘在郡域東南，正是太行山北口與塞內農牧區的交會處。翟松柏起兵之後，郡縣官軍節節後退，起義軍一度連續攻破附近城池。第三方形勢同樣吃重：北面是東突厥。大業十一年冬天，煬帝本人剛被始畢可汗的騎兵包圍在雁門關外，靠雁門一線義民與樊子期的空城計才解圍脫身；到616年，隋對北疆只能靠裴矩主持的招撫與互市維持脆弱平衡。隋廷的主力精騎同年被張須陀帶往山東、河南清剿瓦崗與山東諸部，北方邊線因此空虛。
countriesEn: The two sides in this conflict were the Sui dynasty and the Yanmen rebel army led by Zhai Songbai. At this point Sui was still the largest and wealthiest empire in East Asia, and the political framework built during the Kaihuang era was still standing, but the Daye reign had pushed the state onto a steep slide toward collapse. Emperor Yang of Sui, Yang Guang, had taken the throne in 604 and by 616 had ruled for twelve years; between the capital Luoyang and the eastern capital Jiangdu, his travelling court moved endlessly along the Grand Canal. Sui command was layered in two tiers: at the centre the Ministry of War under the Department of State Affairs held the personnel rolls, the tallies and the written orders, and the field army had travelling army commissioners, commandants and registrars, while at the local level prefects of commanderies and magistrates of counties led commandery and county troops, and the northern frontier commanderies additionally maintained garrison settlers and protective garrisons. By the Daye era the fubing militia system existed in name only: the Kaihuang arrangement of keeping soldiers in the fields and serving the watch in turns had been hollowed out by years of conscription, the treasuries were empty, and deserters had become the main source of recruits, so units mixing hired soldiers with local commandery troops formed the real striking force. On the rebel side was an armed force gathered from the villages, made up mainly of peasants, deserters and loose men from the towns, with a leadership core consisting of Zhai Songbai alone and no recorded staff or general structure. The centre of the rising was Yanmen commandery, whose seat was Yanmen county, in today's Dai County, Shanxi; the commandery administered five counties, Yanmen, Lingqiu, Fanshi, Wutai and Gao, and Lingqiu lay to the southeast of the commandery, precisely where the northern mouth of the Taihang Mountains met the farming and pastoral zone inside the passes. After Zhai raised his banner the commandery and county troops fell back in turn and the rebels managed to break into several neighbouring cities in succession. The situation of a third party weighed just as heavily: to the north lay the Eastern Turkic Khaganate. In the winter of Daye 11 the emperor himself had just been surrounded on the roads outside Yanmen Pass by the horsemen of Shibi Qaghan, and had been released only through the efforts of volunteers along the Yanmen line and Fan Ziqi's ruse of the empty city; by 616 Sui could hold the northern frontier only through the pacification and mutual trade run by Pei Ju, a precarious balance. Meanwhile the Sui's finest cavalry under Zhang Xuetuo was drawn away to Shandong and Henan to suppress the Wagang band and the rebels of the eastern provinces, leaving the northern line thinly held.
people: 翟松柏，雁門郡人，生卒年與出身都不見於史傳。《隋書·帝紀第四》與《北史·隋本紀下》只記他於大業十二年正月初七甲午日在靈丘起兵，聚眾數萬、攻擊周邊郡縣，此外無一字生平。與他同名的瓦崗首領翟讓是東郡韋城人，兩人年代相若而地望懸殊，因為名字相近，後世常把這場雁門起義與瓦崗軍混為一談，這是必須先分清的一點。隋煬帝楊廣是這一場衝突的真正對手，卻不在現場。大業十一年冬他在雁門被東突厥圍困數十日，十二年正月起兵時他已退到洛陽，此後仍沿運河東巡，對雁門的應對只是下詔令郡州討平、發兵捕討，實際指揮落在雁門郡與鄰郡的守將手上。值得留意的是幾個相關人物。樊子期與雲定興是上一年雁門之圍中響應義兵、執意救援皇帝的鄉里人物，說明雁門民間一旦有事就敢以武裝自保，也說明官方對雁門鄉兵的調度並不放心。裴矩主持的對突厥招撫與互市是616年北方邊防的底色，只要邊軍不作叛、商路不斷，雁門的守備就不會被大量抽走，這也解釋了為何起義軍在初期能得到數萬響應而未立即被壓下去。另一端的隋將張須陀同年被瓦崗翟讓、李密擊敗，隋廷最精銳的一支騎兵隊伍被吸在山東與河南，西北線因此捉襟見肘。翟松柏本人的結局、麾下將領姓名、下場如何，正史皆未記載。
peopleEn: Zhai Songbai was a man of Yanmen commandery; neither his dates nor his background appear in any surviving biography. The Book of Sui, Annals of Emperor Yang, and the Bei Shi, Sui annals, record only that on the jiawu day of the seventh day of the first month of Daye 12, that is 616, he raised troops at Lingqiu, gathered tens of thousands of men and attacked the neighbouring commanderies and counties; beyond this not one word of his life is preserved. The Wagang leader of the same name, Zhai Rang, was from Weicheng in Dong commandery: the two men belong to the same period but to widely separated places, and because their names are so close, later writers have constantly confused this Yanmen rising with the Wagang army, and that has to be sorted out first. Emperor Yang of Sui, Yang Guang, was the real opponent in this conflict, yet he was not on the spot. In the winter of Daye 11 he had been shut up at Yanmen by the Eastern Turks for several tens of days; when the rising began in the first month of Daye 12 he had already withdrawn to Luoyang and continued his tour east along the canal. His response to Yanmen was no more than an edict ordering the prefectures and counties to suppress the rebels and post troops to hunt them down, and the actual command fell to the defending officers of Yanmen and the neighbouring commanderies. Several related figures deserve notice. Fan Ziqi and Yun Dingxing were men of the local district who rallied with armed villagers during the Yanmen siege of the previous year and insisted on rescuing the emperor, which shows both that the people of Yanmen would once something happened take up arms on their own account, and that the court was not at ease about how the local militia of Yanmen might be used. Pei Ju's pacification of the Turks and the mutual trade he supervised formed the background of northern defence in 616: as long as the frontier army did not defect and the caravan routes kept running, the garrison of Yanmen would not be stripped away, and this also explains why the rebels could gather tens of thousands in the early days without being crushed at once. On the other front the Sui general Zhang Xuetuo was defeated in the same year by Zhai Rang and Li Mi of the Wagang, so the finest mounted troops in the empire were tied up in Shandong and Henan and the northwestern line was stretched dangerously thin. Zhai Songbai's own fate, the names of his commanders and how the affair ended are all left unrecorded by the official histories.
kits: 卡面這件秦連弩是這場邊郡起義裡最貼合的兵器。連弩以弩機儲存拉力，上弦一次便可連續踩踏發射，不必每次重拉弓弦；秦時已有成熟弩機出土，漢代馬援奏請造連弩、自稱一發十矢，魏晉南北朝各代沿用不輟，到隋代仍是守城、扼隘、伏擊時的常備器械，與大型床弩、弓兵搭配使用。它在雁門戰線上能派上用場，理由很實際。靈丘、五台、繁畤之間是太行北段的山地與河谷，道路狹窄，騎兵難以展開，官軍的攻城器械雲梯、撞車、巢車也難以在碎石坡上運作；守方居高臨下，以連續射擊的弩雨壓住密集的進攻隊形，一踩一發的射速意味著短時間內能傾瀉大量箭矢，正是把衝鋒隊形壓在牆外、壓在隘口之外的辦法。反過來說，連弩的弱點也在這裡：弩機結構細密，沙泥入機便難以復原，上弦儲力一旦被人撞斷便全無用處，破甲力與射程也遠不及大弩。起義軍自身的裝備更為樸素，絕大多數人只有削尖的木杆長矛、環首刀、耙叉與漁叉，皮甲布甲極為稀少，戰車器械幾乎沒有，靠的是鄉里熟悉山道、數量眾多。隋軍一側則是弓弩混編的步卒加上騎兵，攻城時備雲梯、撞車、巢車與火箭，傳訊靠雁門邊塞的烽燧台逐段傳警，糧秣靠畜力與人力沿滹沱河谷與山道北運。
kitsEn: The repeating crossbow on the card is the weapon that fits this frontier rising most closely. A repeating crossbow stores its draw in the lock, so that once it is cocked the bow can be fired repeatedly by treading the trigger, and the archer need not draw the string again for every shot. Mature crossbow locks survive from the Qin period; in Han times Ma Yuan petitioned to build repeating crossbows and described them as loosing ten bolts at a stroke; the Wei, Jin and the northern and southern dynasties carried the type on without interruption, and in Sui it remained a standard piece of equipment for defending walls, choking passes and lying in ambush, used alongside the heavy bed crossbow and the ordinary bow. The reason it could be put to work on the Yanmen line is a practical one. Between Lingqiu, Wutai and Fanshi lie the mountains and river valleys of the northern Taihang range: the roads are narrow, cavalry cannot deploy, and the siege engines of the Sui army, scaling ladders, battering rams and siege towers, are equally hard to haul over a scree slope. The defenders, looking down from the heights, meet the dense attacking formation with a rain of bolts delivered in rapid succession, and the speed of the tread-launched repeating crossbow means a great many arrows can be poured out in a short space of time; that is precisely the way to pin a charging formation outside the wall and outside the mouth of the pass. The weaknesses of the weapon are the mirror image of its strengths: the lock is finely made and once sand or mud works into it the mechanism is hard to restore, and if the stored tension is broken by a blow the piece is useless; its armour-piercing power and range are also far below those of the great crossbows. The rebels' own equipment was far plainer: the great majority had only sharpened wooden-shaft spears, ring-pommel sabres, pitchforks and fishing spears; hide and cloth armour were extremely scarce, and they had almost no wagons or siege machines, relying instead on numbers and on locals who knew every mountain path. On the Sui side were foot soldiers drawn from bow and crossbow units mixed together, supported by cavalry; for assaults they brought scaling ladders, battering rams, siege towers and fire arrows; signalling ran by the beacon towers of the Yanmen frontier, passing the alarm stage by stage; and the grain and provisions were moved north by pack animals and porters along the Hutuo valley and the mountain roads.
tactics: 起義軍的戰法是典型的鄉民武裝起事：以靈丘縣城為核心，先集結後散開，聚散之間靠鄉里網絡與熟悉地形的山民嚮導。起兵初期人數直上數萬，採取的是流動打擊而非固守：一部沿東側平型關通道向蔚州方向窺探，一部沿北面窄谷逼近繁畤與雁門縣，一部南取五台與崞縣方向，切斷郡治與汾晉平原之間的糧道。隊伍多帶三日乾糧，靠田間搶收與村寨徵集維持給養，沒有攻城器械，遇到城池多數只作圍擾與襲取，並不強攻。起義軍極少有馬匹，快速的傳令與追擊無力，一旦離開山地、進入平原與官軍主力接觸，便難以維持人數與陣形。隋軍一側則以郡兵與募兵混編的隊伍為主，自雁門關與太原晉陽兩個方向合進，沿官道與山谷路南下，把兵分成前鋒、弩手隊與預備隊，據城禦守時以城頭弩陣壓制，野戰時用騎兵兩翼包抄。圍城與斷糧是對付流動起義的標準辦法：斷掉靈丘與鄉村之間的運糧小徑，再以四面合圍收緊，逼起義軍在缺乏糧秣與彈藥時出來決戰。連弩正是在城頭與隘口反覆使用的器械，射速快而射擊連續，足以在官軍尚未合圍之前先把進攻方的前鋒壓退。整場衝突的細節，例如雙方具體的進攻次序、陣形編組與傷亡數字，正史都沒有留下記載，只能從地勢、兵制與兵器的限制去推想。
tacticsEn: The way the rebels fought was that of a typical rising of village armed men: the county seat of Lingqiu was the core, and they first concentrated and then dispersed, moving and meeting again through the network of village ties and through local guides who knew the ground. In the first days the numbers swelled straight to tens of thousands, and what they practised was mobile striking rather than holding ground. One part probed eastward along the Pingxing Pass route toward the Yu prefecture, one part climbed the narrow northern valleys toward Fanshi and Yanmen county, and one part moved south toward Wutai and Gao county, cutting the grain road between the commandery seat and the Fen and Jin plains. The bands carried about three days of dry rations and lived off what they took from the fields and gathered from the villages; they had no siege engines, and when they met a walled town they mostly surrounded it, harassed it and struck by surprise rather than delivering a real assault. Having very few horses, they could not pass orders quickly or pursue, and once they left the hills and came into contact with the main body of the Sui army on the plain they could not hold their numbers or their formation. The Sui army, on the other hand, worked from units mixing commandery soldiers with hired men, advancing on two axes from Yanmen Pass and from the Jinyang area of Taiyuan, moving south along the official roads and the valley tracks, and dividing into vanguard, crossbow companies and a reserve. When they sat in a walled town they used the crossbow line on the wall to bear down on the attackers; in the field they used cavalry on both wings to envelop. Besieging and cutting supplies was the standard answer to a mobile rising: sever the small grain paths between Lingqiu and the villages, then tighten the noose from four sides, forcing the rebels out to fight when they had neither provisions nor ammunition left. The repeating crossbow was exactly the piece used again and again from the wall and the pass, fast in rate of fire and continuous in shooting, more than enough to push back the attackers' vanguard before the Sui columns had even closed. The finer details of the fighting, such as the actual order of attack on both sides, the grouping of formations and the casualty figures, are not preserved in the official histories, and can only be inferred from the terrain, the military system and the limits of the weapons.
data: 有據可查的數字不多，逐一列出。時間：大業十二年正月初七甲午日，即616年農曆正月初七，翟松柏於靈丘起兵。兵力：正史記聚眾數萬，這是唯一的兵數記載，數萬之眾屬概數，無法拆分為步騎，也無法核算到各縣。行政：起兵地雁門郡下轄五縣，郡治雁門縣在今山西代縣，靈丘、五台、崞、繁畤分列東南。距離：靈丘縣城到平型關約四十公里，到五台縣城約七十公里，到繁畤約八十公里，到崞縣即今原平崞陽一帶約一百五十公里，到郡治雁門縣約一百四十公里，到太原晉陽約二百五十公里。地形：靈丘位於太行北段，平均海拔在千米以上，谷道狹窄，冬季積雪封山，限制了騎兵與車兵的展開速度。可作對照的國家層面數字是隋的戰爭負荷：開皇末到大業年間，隋三次征高句麗，每次發兵以數十萬計，役使與徵發遍及河北、山東、江南，府兵編制在十餘年內被抽空；616年時全國實際能戰的兵源相對有限，邊郡的守備多靠臨時徵發與募兵。平叛的時間、官軍的具體兵額與雙方戰損，正史都沒有記載，現代研究也只能以同年內平定一語概括這場短促的邊亂。
dataEn: The figures that can actually be vouched for are few, and they are set out one by one. Date: the jiawu day of the seventh day of the first month of Daye 12, that is the seventh day of the first lunar month of 616, when Zhai Songbai raised his troops at Lingqiu. Numbers: the official histories record that he gathered tens of thousands of men; this is the only troop figure preserved, it is a round number, and it cannot be broken down into foot and horse or apportioned among the counties. Administration: the commandery in which the rising began, Yanmen, administered five counties; its seat, Yanmen county, lies in today's Dai County, Shanxi, while Lingqiu, Wutai, Gao and Fanshi lay off to the southeast. Distances: from the county seat of Lingqiu about forty kilometres to Pingxing Pass, about seventy to the seat of Wutai county, about eighty to Fanshi, about a hundred and fifty to Gao county in today's Yuanping at Huoyang, about a hundred and forty to the commandery seat of Yanmen county, and about two hundred and fifty to Jinyang in Taiyuan. Terrain: Lingqiu lies in the northern section of the Taihang range at an average elevation above a thousand metres, the valley tracks are narrow, and in winter the passes close under snow, which restricts how fast cavalry and wagon trains can deploy. The national-scale figures that can be set against this are the Sui's war burden: from the end of the Kaihuang era through the Daye reign, Sui campaigned against Goguryeo three times, each time raising armies numbered in the tens of thousands, with the levies and corvées reaching Hebei, Shandong and the south; the fubing establishment was drained away within a dozen years. By 616 the country had relatively little manpower that could still fight, and the frontier commanderies relied mostly on ad hoc levies and hired soldiers. The time taken to suppress the rising, the exact strength of the Sui columns and the casualties on both sides are all absent from the histories, and modern work can only summarise this short frontier disturbance as having been put down within the same year.
cause: 直接導火線是616年正月初七靈丘的聚眾，但根源在三徵高句麗之後國力急劇透支的隋朝。開皇時期留下的府兵與糧倉體系，本來足以支撐一次大規模邊防行動，大業朝卻把它們連年透支：西征吐谷渾、南巡江都、三征高句麗，每次都徵發大批丁壯，河北山東的民戶被拉走，逃戶成為社會常態，糧價與役負同時上升。邊郡的處境更為惡劣，靈丘、繁畤一線既要供應邊軍的軍糧與轉輸，又要承受州縣額外的攤派，戶口大量流散，鄉里之間的互助與衝突都到了臨界點。民間層面還有另一股推力。隋末讖語與歌謠在河南、河北、山西一帶流傳，講的是劉氏當有天下一類的預言，百姓把兵亂、災荒與讖語連在一起解讀，於是起兵者只要打起旗號，響應的人就會很快聚集。地方上豪族與遊俠的武裝傳統同樣存在，晉北、雁門一線民間多有私兵與獵戶，關係到山道、糧倉與城守的關鍵位置一旦失守，官府對鄉里的控制就會迅速崩解。把這些放在一起看，616年的雁門起義不是孤立的治安事件，而是一場已經席捲山東河北、正在向北方邊郡蔓延的隋末民變浪潮的一個節點。同一年，瓦崗的翟讓與後來投奔的李密在河南擊敗隋將張須陀，江淮地區也有杜伏威等部眾舉旗，山西與河北之間的邊地因此被隋廷視為可以調度的地方，卻恰恰是最脆弱的一環。
causeEn: The immediate trigger was the gathering of men at Lingqiu on the seventh day of the first month of 616, but the root lay in the Sui state whose strength had been catastrophically overdrawn by the three campaigns against Goguryeo. The fubing system and the storehouses of the Kaihuang era had been sufficient to sustain a single large frontier operation, but the Daye reign drew on them year after year: the western expedition against Tuyuhun, the southern tours to Jiangdu, the three campaigns against Goguryeo, each of them dragging away great numbers of labouring men, emptying the households of Hebei and Shandong, making flight a permanent feature of life, and pushing up both the price of grain and the weight of corvée. The situation of the frontier commanderies was worse still: the Lingqiu and Fanshi line had to supply the grain and the transport of the frontier army while also bearing additional levies from the prefectures, the population was scattered widely, and both the mutual aid and the friction of village society had reached a breaking point. At the level of popular belief there was a second push. Prophecies and songs in the late Sui circulated through Henan, Hebei and Shanxi, telling of a prophecy that a house surnamed Liu would hold the realm, and the common people read rebellion, famine and prophecy together, so that once a rebel raised a banner the response came quickly. The armed tradition of local great families and wandering swordsmen mattered as well: in northern Shanxi and along the Yanmen line there were private bands and hunters, and once the positions that mattered for the mountain roads, the granaries and the defence of the towns fell, the government's hold over the countryside broke down at once. Taken together, the Yanmen rising of 616 was not an isolated policing matter but a single node in a wave of late Sui popular revolts that had already swept across Shandong and Hebei and was now spreading toward the northern frontier commanderies. In the same year Zhai Rang of the Wagang and Li Mi, who came over to him later, defeated the Sui general Zhang Xuetuo in Henan, and in the Jianghuai region other bands rose under men such as Du Fuwei. The borderland between Shanxi and Hebei was therefore treated by the Sui court as a region it could shift troops through, and it was precisely the most fragile link in the chain.
impact: 就眼前的軍局而言，這場起義的規模有限：起兵聚眾數萬，據《隋書》與《北史》本紀的概略記載，亂事在隋軍討伐下平定，靈丘一線的郡縣秩序短暫恢復。它沒有像瓦崗那樣拖住隋廷的主力，也沒有形成割據一方的政權。但放在隋末十幾年的長線裡看，這場起義的意義不次於一次大勝。616年正是隋朝在山東、河北四面失血、在河南被瓦崗拖住、在雁門被突厥逼退的同一年，北方邊郡一旦響應，就等於宣告隋廷對地方的控制只剩下一層薄殼。為了平掉這樣的小規模邊亂，朝廷照例要加發兵役、就地徵集、賞格捕殺，每平一處亂事就再刮一層地皮，府兵與民戶的崩解因此加速，隋朝在兩年之後亡國的結局，正是從這一連串看似可以一一平息的起義裡累積出來的。另一層影響是地理上的。雁門與代北是關內通往塞北的孔道，隋朝平叛之後留下的兵源空缺，使得北方的守備線一直薄弱，隨即被李淵集團與劉武周所利用：617年劉武周起兵於馬邑，數月之間攻下太原，619年南下攻陷晉陽，雁門、代北這一線再成戰場，隋末的天下爭奪正是從這條線上打開缺口。最後是記憶的層面。翟松柏的名字在傳世文獻裡只留下兩三行，正史不載其人其事於細節，後人往往將他與瓦崗的翟讓混為一人，連雁門起義與瓦崗軍也常被並在一起講。一場改變了山西北部十年間走向的邊亂，幾乎從歷史敘述裡消失。
impactEn: As far as the immediate military situation was concerned, the rising was of limited scale: it gathered tens of thousands of men, and according to the summary notices in the annals of the Book of Sui and the Bei Shi the disturbance was put down by Sui troops, and order in the commanderies and counties along the Lingqiu line was briefly restored. It did not pin the main strength of the Sui court the way the Wagang band did, and it never formed a power of its own. But set against the long arc of the last fifteen years of the Sui, its significance was no less than that of a great victory. 616 was the year in which the Sui was bleeding on four fronts at once, in Shandong and Hebei, held down in Henan by the Wagang band and driven back from Yanmen by the Turks; for the northern frontier commanderies to rise in answer was to declare that the court's control over the localities had been reduced to a thin shell. To put down a disturbance of this size, the court did what it always did, adding levies, gathering men on the spot and offering rewards for captures, and every rebellion that was suppressed meant one more layer scraped off the peasantry; the breakdown of the fubing system and of the rural households was thereby accelerated, and the Sui's destruction two years later was accumulated out of this long sequence of risings each of which seemed capable of being settled one at a time. There is a second layer of consequence, and it is geographic. Yanmen and northern Dai were the corridor by which the interior of the empire connected with the steppe, and the gap in manpower left behind by the suppression kept the northern defensive line thin, a gap that was promptly used by the Li Yuan group and by Liu Wuzhou: in 617 Liu Wuzhou raised troops at Mayi, took Taiyuan within a few months, and in 619 marched south and seized Jinyang, so that the Yanmen and northern Dai line became a battlefield once more, and the contest for the empire in the late Sui was opened precisely along this corridor. Last there is the layer of memory. The name of Zhai Songbai survives in the transmitted literature in two or three lines only; the official histories record nothing of his person or his deeds in detail; later writers constantly merge him with Zhai Rang of the Wagang, and even the Yanmen rising and the Wagang army are often told as one and the same business. A frontier rising that changed the course of northern Shanxi for a decade very nearly disappeared from the historical narrative.
result: 結果是起義被平定，但平定的過程幾乎沒有留下文字。現存最直接的兩條記載是《隋書》卷四《帝紀第四·炀帝下》與《北史》卷十二《隋本紀下》，兩處都只是寥寥數語：正月初七甲午日，雁門郡人翟松柏起兵於靈丘，聚眾數萬，相繼攻打附近郡縣，隨後為隋軍所討平。統兵討平者的姓名、出兵的路線、交戰的地點、斬獲與亡失的數目，兩部史書都沒有記載，《資治通鑑》編纂時也只是概括帶過，並未展開戰鬥經過。因此可以確定的結果有三項：其一，起義軍在同年之內被消滅，靈丘與鄰近各縣恢復郡縣編制，雁門關的烽燧傳訊與城防重新運作；其二，翟松柏本人及其部眾的下場不明，史料既沒有記載他被擒或被誅，也沒有記載他逃散山林，只留下名字與起兵日期；其三，亂事雖平，隋朝在山西河北的統治形勢並沒有因此穩住，反而把更多丁壯抽進兵役，把更多郡縣推入起義的循環。把時間軸拉開，起義被平的那一年，正是隋朝全面崩解的序曲。617年竇建德在河北、劉武周在太原、瓦崗李密在中原分別建號，618年隋煬帝在江都遇弑，隋恭帝在長安讓位，長安、洛陽兩地先後易主。翟松柏的起義本身沒有改寫任何一次政權更替，但它落實了一個事實：到了616年，隋朝的邊郡已經可以用數萬之眾一夜之間集結起來，而這樣的起義在一年之內可以出現很多次，每一次都要用兵役去平，每一次都讓中央更虛弱。
resultEn: The result was that the rising was put down, but the process of putting it down left almost no written record. The two most direct notices that survive are in the Book of Sui, juan four, Annals of Emperor Yang, lower part, and in the Bei Shi, juan twelve, Sui annals, lower part, and both are only a few lines: on the jiawu day of the seventh day of the first month, Zhai Songbai of Yanmen commandery raised troops at Lingqiu, gathered tens of thousands of men, and one after another attacked the neighbouring commanderies and counties, whereupon the rising was suppressed by Sui troops. The name of the commander who did the suppressing, the route the troops marched, the place where they fought, and the numbers taken or lost are recorded in neither history, and when the Comprehensive Mirror compiled its account it only carried the matter in broad strokes without setting out the course of the fighting. Three things can therefore be stated with certainty. First, the rebel force was destroyed within that same year, Lingqiu and the neighbouring counties were brought back under commandery and county administration, and the beacon signalling and the defences of Yanmen Pass began to work again. Second, the fate of Zhai Songbai himself and of his followers is unknown: the sources record neither his capture nor his execution, nor any scattering of his men into the hills, and leave only his name and the date of the rising. Third, although the disturbance was settled, the Sui's hold over Shanxi and Hebei did not thereby steady; on the contrary more and more labouring men were drawn into the levies and more and more commanderies were pushed into the cycle of revolt. Drawn out on a longer timeline, the year in which this rising was put down was the overture to the complete dissolution of the Sui. In 617 Dou Jiande raised his title in Hebei, Liu Wuzhou in Taiyuan and Li Mi of the Wagang in the central plain; in 618 Emperor Yang of Sui was killed at Jiangdu and the Sui gong emperor yielded the throne at Chang'an, so that Chang'an and Luoyang changed hands one after the other. The rising of Zhai Songbai by itself rewrote no single transfer of power, but it settled a point of fact: by 616 the frontier commanderies of the Sui could raise tens of thousands of men in the space of a single night, and such risings could occur many times within a year, each of them requiring levies to put down, and each of them leaving the centre weaker.
